title: Conspiracy Without Theory? Exploring the Past and Present of Conspiratorial Thinking
desc:
Throughout many historical periods, conspiracy theories have exerted an influence in societies and been manipulated for their own purposes by those in power. Recent controversies over climate change, vaccines, telecommunications, media and more, have given rise to concepts such as the ‘deep state’, ‘the establishment’, and ‘globalists’.

Often fuelled by social media, these newer claims are often so shallow and impulsive that they’ve been branded as ‘conspiracism’; that is, ‘conspiracy without the theory’. As Muirhead and Rosenblum (2019) explain, ‘conspiracy without the theory dispenses with the burden of explanation. We see no insistent demand for proof, no exhaustive amassing of evidence, no dots revealed to form a pattern, no close examination of the operators plotting in the…

title: CLAW: AI in Science Seminar Series – Building AI Research Partners: Connecting Scientific Knowledge, Ideas and Experiments with Professor Yulan He
desc:
Abstract:

Large language models are increasingly used to support scientific research, but challenges remain in developing reliable AI research partners. Scientific literature exploration needs to move beyond semantic similarity, since meaningful discoveries often emerge from connecting seemingly unrelated work through shared problems or transferable methods. Novelty assessment requires grounding scientific claims in structured evidence and prior work. Research reproducibility is hindered by incomplete descriptions and omissions of implementation details in papers. In this talk, I will discuss our recent work addressing these challenges, including graph-distilled generative retrieval enabling literature discovery beyond similarity-based search; bi-level graph reasoning for…

title: Junior Dynamics Seminar – Fraser Sanders (University of Manchester)
desc:
Infinite-dimensional contact geometry and conservative contact systems

Speaker: Fraser Sanders (University of Manchester)

Abstract : In finite dimensions, contact geometry is well-studied as an odd-dimensional counterpart to symplectic geometry. It is also a natural setting in which to generalise Hamiltonian mechanics of systems, taking into account a notion of dissipation or diffusion. For example, the simplest example of a contact-Hamiltonian system is the damped harmonic oscillator (the dissipative counterpart to the simple harmonic oscillator). Due to the diffusive properties of the contact-Hamilton equations, it is also a natural setting in which to study thermodynamics (cf. Grmela, Bravetti, and many others). title: PDEs Seminar – Andrea Zanoni ( University of Pisa)
desc:
Title: Inverse problems for a coupled parabolic-elliptic PDE system

Abstract: Inverse problems arising from coupled partial differential equations pose significant analytical challenges, particularly when unknown coefficients influence the observed quantities only indirectly. In this talk, we investigate the recovery of a spatially varying permittivity in a coupled Fokker-Planck-Darcy system from discrete, noisy observations of the Fokker-Planck solution. The unknown coefficient enters the elliptic Darcy equation, while observations are available only through the coupled parabolic equation. We establish well-posedness and a priori estimates for the underlying PDE system, together with stability estimates for the associated inverse problem. Building on these analytical results, we study…

title: SIAM Junior Applied Mathematics Seminar (JAMS) – Philipp Plank & Dr Samantha Linn
desc:
Learning Distributed Equilibria in Linear-Quadratic Stochastic Differential Games: An alpha-Potential Approach

Speaker 1: Philip Plank

Abstract: This talk analyses independent policy-gradient learning in N-player linear-quadratic stochastic differential games. Each player employs a distributed policy that depends only on its own state and updates its policy independently by following the gradient of its own objective. We show that the game admits an alpha-potential structure, where alpha is determined by the degree of pairwise interaction asymmetry. Exploiting this structure, we establish global linear convergence of these methods to an approximate equilibrium, with suboptimality proportional to the degree of asymmetry and complexity scaling approximately linearly with the population…
